served.stem: What volume does 3 mol of an ideal gas occupy at 227 °C and 0.5 atm? (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K)

answer.line: At 500 K and 0.5 atm one mole fills 82.1 L, so three moles fill three times that: 246 L.

steps: Find one mole's room: RT / P = 0.0821 x 500 / 0.5 = 82.1 L. Hot, thin gas is big.
Three moles take three times the room: 3 x 82.1 = 246 L.

choices.note: 82.1 L is the room one mole takes at these conditions. The stem has three moles.
3 x 0.0821 x 227 / 0.5 is about 112. Gas laws need kelvin, 500 K here.
R = 8.314 goes with joules and pascals. With liters and atm, R is 0.0821.
This multiplies by 0.5 atm instead of dividing. Lower pressure lets the gas spread out, so P goes underneath.

student.lockIt: V = nRT / P, with T in kelvin and R = 0.0821 for liters and atm.
